content.text: In countries like Zimbabwe, where platforms like Stripe and PayPal are severely restricted, digital creators face a significant challenge in setting up online stores that accept crypto payments. This is where COREMERCH comes in, offering a sovereign commerce infrastructure that enables creators to deploy their own digital stores on platforms like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, with automatic crypto payment processing and full data ownership. This guide will walk you through building a crypto store on Cloudflare Pages, highlighting the key differences between Stack 01 and Stack 02.
Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The COREMERCH infrastructure is designed to be platform-agnostic, allowing creators to deploy their stores on GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, and process payments through NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies. This approach eliminates the dependence on restrictive platforms, giving creators full control over their stores and customer data. With Stack 01, you can deploy a basic store on GitHub Pages, while Stack 02 offers a more advanced setup on Cloudflare Pages, with additional features like Supabase for order storage and Workers for backend logic.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your crypto store, you need to have a clear understanding of your product offerings, target audience, and marketing strategy. You also need to set up a NOWPayments account, which will handle the crypto payment processing for your store. Additionally, you need to choose between Stack 01 and Stack 02, depending on your specific needs and technical expertise. Stack 01 is a more straightforward setup, while Stack 02 requires more configuration and setup, but offers more advanced features and scalability.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Once you have your store setup, you need to configure your payment and delivery pipeline. This involves setting up NOWPayments to receive crypto payments, and configuring your store to deliver digital products automatically upon payment confirmation. With Stack 02, you also need to set up Supabase for order storage, and configure Workers to handle backend logic. This may require some technical expertise, but the end result is a seamless and automated payment and delivery process.
Deploy your store on Cloudflare Pages for advanced features and scalability.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

After setting up your store and payment pipeline, you can go live and start processing transactions. This involves testing your store on the mainnet, to ensure that everything is working as expected. You should also have a clear understanding of how to handle customer support, and how to troubleshoot any issues that may arise. With Stack 02, you also need to configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC to ensure email deliverability, and test your store end-to-end to ensure a smooth customer experience.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

Once your store is up and running, you can focus on scaling your business. This involves optimizing your store for performance, and expanding your product offerings and marketing reach. With Stack 02, you can leverage the advanced features of Cloudflare Pages and Supabase to handle increased traffic and sales, and use the scaling playbook provided with The Sovereign Blueprint to ensure a smooth and profitable growth trajectory.
